prerequisites.title: Kintone system administrator access
prerequisites.detail: The OAuth client is created from User & System Administration, under System Administration, then OAuth.

prerequisites.title: Bring your own client credentials in Composio
prerequisites.detail: Composio has no managed Kintone app, so create the auth config with your own client ID and secret.

steps.title: Choose scopes for your agent
steps.detail: Pick the minimum scopes, for example k:app_record:read and k:app_record:write. Separate multiple scopes with spaces.
inputs: List of Kintone actions the agent needs

steps.title: Copy redirect URI from Composio dashboard
steps.detail: Copy the callback URL shown in the Composio dashboard for the Kintone REST toolkit.

steps.title: Register the OAuth client in Kintone
steps.detail: As admin, click Add OAuth Client, enter the client name, optional logo and the required redirect endpoint, then save.
steps.done_when: Client ID and secret are shown

steps.title: Enable users for the client
steps.detail: Use Configure users to check each user who may use the client.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create the auth config through Composio's API with your client ID and secret for the kintone_rest toolkit.

steps.title: Test a connection end to end
steps.detail: Connect a test user, approve the authorization request, then make a REST call within the granted scopes.

traps.title: Users are disabled by default
traps.detail: A newly registered client works for nobody until users are checked, and each new Kintone user starts unchecked.

traps.title: IP-restricted domains block OAuth
traps.detail: OAuth client features cannot be used from domains with IP restrictions unless the client's IP is allowlisted. Ask each customer about this.

traps.title: Access tokens last one hour
traps.detail: Access tokens expire after 1 hour and expired codes or tokens return errors, so refresh tokens must be used. Authorization codes last 10 minutes.

traps.title: Client and refresh token limits
traps.detail: A domain can register up to 20 OAuth clients, and one client can hold up to 10 refresh tokens per user.

blockers.symptom: Users cannot authorize or API calls fail for a user
blockers.what_it_means: The user may not be enabled for the OAuth client, or the token lacks the needed scope.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the admin to check the user in Configure users, and request the required scopes.
blockers.agent_can_help: Compare the failing API call with the scope list and suggest missing scopes.
